passages.text: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
passages.sermon:
God gives us great promises.
We are God's beloved people.
We have these promises from God.
Let us remove everything that makes our bodies unclean.
Let us remove everything that makes our spirits unclean.
Let us make ourselves pure.
Let us become holy.
Let us do this with reverence for God.
passages.original: Ταύτας οὖν ἔχοντες τὰς ἐπαγγελίας ἀγαπητοί καθαρίσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς μολυσμοῦ σαρκὸς καὶ πνεύματος ἐπιτελοῦντες ἁγιωσύνην ἐν φόβῳ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
Paul asks them to make room for him and his companions in their hearts.
Paul says, “We have wronged no one.”
Paul says, “We have corrupted no one.”
Paul says, “We have exploited no one.”
passages.original: Χωρήσατε ἡμᾶς οὐδένα ἠδικήσαμεν οὐδένα ἐφθείραμεν οὐδένα ἐπλεονεκτήσαμεν

passages.text: I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.
passages.sermon:
I do not say this to condemn you.
You are in our hearts.
We live together with you.
We would die together with you.
passages.original: πρὸς κατάκρισιν οὐ λέγω προείρηκα γὰρ ὅτι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν ἐστε εἰς τὸ συναποθανεῖν καὶ συζῆν

passages.text: Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian church.
\r\nPaul feels great confidence in the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul feels great pride in the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul is filled with encouragement.
\r\nPaul has many troubles.
\r\nPaul’s joy overflows in all his troubles.
passages.original: πολλή μοι παρρησία πρὸς ὑμᾶς πολλή μοι καύχησις ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν πεπλήρωμαι τῇ παρακλήσει ὑπερπερισσεύομαι τῇ χαρᾷ ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν

passages.text: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions arrived in Macedonia.
Their bodies found no rest.
They faced trouble everywhere.
They experienced conflicts on the outside.
They felt fears on the inside.
passages.original: Καὶ γὰρ ἐλθόντων ἡμῶν εἰς Μακεδονίαν οὐδεμίαν ἔσχηκεν ἄνεσιν ἡ σὰρξ ἡμῶν ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ θλιβόμενοι ἔξωθεν μάχαι ἔσωθεν φόβοι

passages.text: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus, and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
passages.sermon:
God comforts people who are downcast.
God comforted us.
God did this when Titus arrived.
God did not comfort us only by Titus’s arrival.
God also comforted us through the encouragement Titus received from you.
Titus told us about your longing for me.
Titus told us about your mourning.
Titus told us about your zeal for me.
Because of this, I rejoiced even more.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὁ παρακαλῶν τοὺς ταπεινοὺς παρεκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ Τίτου οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ᾗ παρεκλήθη ἐφ’ ὑμῖν ἀναγγέλλων ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἐπιπόθησιν τὸν ὑμῶν ὀδυρμόν τὸν ὑμῶν ζῆλον ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ ὥστε με μᾶλλον χαρῆναι

passages.text: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it, I now see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time.
passages.sermon:
I wrote you a letter.
My letter caused you sorrow.
I do not regret writing it.
At first, I did regret it.
Now I see something clearly.
My letter made you sad for only a short time.
passages.original: Ὅτι εἰ καὶ ἐλύπησα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ οὐ μεταμέλομαι εἰ καὶ μετεμελόμην βλέπω γὰρ ὅτι ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἐκείνη εἰ καὶ πρὸς ὥραν ἐλύπησεν ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul feels joy now.
\r\nHe does not rejoice because the Corinthians were made sorrowful.
\r\nHe rejoices because their sorrow led them to repentance.
\r\nTheir sorrow was the kind that God intended.
\r\nBecause of this, they were not harmed by Paul or his companions in any way.
passages.original: νῦν χαίρω οὐχ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐλυπήθητε εἰς μετάνοιαν ἐλυπήθητε γὰρ κατὰ Θεόν ἵνα ἐν μηδενὶ ζημιωθῆτε ἐξ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
passages.sermon:
Godly sorrow produces repentance.
This repentance leads to salvation.
This salvation brings no regret.
Worldly sorrow produces death.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ κατὰ Θεὸν λύπη μετάνοιαν εἰς σωτηρίαν ἀμεταμέλητον ἐργάζεται ἡ δὲ τοῦ κόσμου λύπη θάνατον κατεργάζεται

passages.text: Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
passages.sermon:
Godly sorrow comes from God.
Godly sorrow has worked in you.
Godly sorrow has produced earnestness in you.
Godly sorrow has produced eagerness in you to clear yourselves.
Godly sorrow has produced indignation in you.
Godly sorrow has produced fear in you.
Godly sorrow has produced longing in you.
Godly sorrow has produced zeal in you.
Godly sorrow has produced a desire for justice in you.
You have shown yourselves to be innocent in this matter in every way.
passages.original: Ἰδοὺ γὰρ αὐτὸ τοῦτο τὸ κατὰ Θεὸν λυπηθῆναι πόσην κατειργάσατο ὑμῖν σπουδήν ἀλλὰ ἀπολογίαν ἀλλὰ ἀγανάκτησιν ἀλλὰ φόβον ἀλλὰ ἐπιπόθησιν ἀλλὰ ζῆλον ἀλλὰ ἐκδίκησιν ἐν παντὶ συνεστήσατε ἑαυτοὺς ἁγνοὺς εἶναι τῷ πράγματι

passages.text: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote a letter to the Corinthians.
Paul did not write because of the person who did wrong.
Paul did not write because of the person who was harmed.
Paul wrote so that the Corinthians would see their own earnestness for Paul and his companions.
Paul wanted their earnestness to be clear to them.
Paul wanted this to happen before God.
passages.original: ἄρα εἰ καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν οὐχ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικήσαντος οὐδὲ ἕνεκεν τοῦ ἀδικηθέντος ἀλλ’ ἕνεκεν τοῦ φανερωθῆναι τὴν σπουδὴν ὑμῶν τὴν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: On account of this, we are encouraged. In addition to our own encouragement, we were even more delighted by the joy of Titus. For his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
passages.sermon:
We are encouraged because of this.
We also received encouragement ourselves.
We became even more joyful because Titus was joyful.
All of you refreshed his spirit.
Titus felt renewed by you.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο παρακεκλήμεθα Ἐπὶ δὲ τῇ παρακλήσει ἡμῶν περισσοτέρως μᾶλλον ἐχάρημεν ἐπὶ τῇ χαρᾷ Τίτου ὅτι ἀναπέπαυται τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ πάντων ὑμῶν

passages.text: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul spoke to Titus about the Corinthian believers.
Paul boasted to Titus about the Corinthian believers.
Paul was not embarrassed by anything he boasted to Titus about them.
Everything Paul said to the Corinthian believers was true.
Paul’s boasting to Titus was also true.
Paul’s words and his boasting both proved to be true.
passages.original: ὅτι εἴ τι αὐτῷ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κεκαύχημαι οὐ κατῃσχύνθην ἀλλ’ ὡς πάντα ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ἐλαλήσαμεν ὑμῖν οὕτως καὶ ἡ καύχησις ἡμῶν ἡ ἐπὶ Τίτου ἀλήθεια ἐγενήθη

passages.text: And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
passages.sermon:
Titus feels deep affection for you.
His affection for you grows even more.
He remembers your obedience.
You welcomed him.
You received him with fear and trembling.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς ἐστιν ἀναμιμνῃσκομένου τὴν πάντων ὑμῶν ὑπακοήν ὡς μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου ἐδέξασθε αὐτόν

passages.text: I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul feels joy.
\r\nPaul has complete confidence in you.
\r\nPaul rejoices because he trusts you in every way.
passages.original: χαίρω ὅτι ἐν παντὶ θαρρῶ ἐν ὑμῖν
